Not relieved by Ibuprofen. No nausea, vomiting, vision changes, phonophobia, neck stiffness, rash, or fevers. Mother has migraines and hypertension.
- Reasoning: Headache characteristics (throbbing, unilateral, severe, family history of migraine) suggest a first presentation migraine, though absence of associated symptoms and age of first onset are atypical.

  - Tension-type headache: Low likelihood; pain characteristics are inconsistent.
- Working diagnosis: Migraine (first presentation) — supported by clinical features and family history.
- Considerations: Secondary headache (brain mass, venous thrombosis) should be considered if new symptoms develop or headache persists/worsens despite management.
- Management: Advised stronger pain relief (unspecified; to be taken regularly with food, not concurrently with ibuprofen), rest, hydration. Safety-netting—advised to seek care if symptoms worsen or new symptoms (fever, vomiting, neck stiffness, rash, neurological changes) develop.
